prerequisites: Knowledge from basic subjects (Mathematics, Physics, Graphic Expression)
Specific knowledge from subjects such as Machine Calculation and Design

learning_outcomes.text: Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and their clear and concise presentation.
Aptitude for the distribution of resources and time and their implementation in real situations.
Ability to use scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for finding sustainable engineering solutions.
Ability for teamwork and ability to develop multidisciplinary projects.
Knowledge and abilities for the calculation, design and testing of machines.

syllabus_topics: TOPIC I Introduction. -Review of previous concepts: shaft design, power and connecting screws, mechanical springs

TOPIC II Gears - Basic concepts on dimensions and fundamental values of gears. Review - Geometry of gears. Review - Definition of geometry - Cutting angles and reference circles - Types of gear tooth profiles - Involute profile, rolling without slipping - Contact ratio

TOPIC III Forces and angles in gear teeth - Tangential, radial and axial force. - Relationship between forces and construction and cutting angles - Stresses and strains in the base section of a gear tooth - Transmitted power.
TOPIC IV Tribology and lubrication - Introduction - Friction - Wear - Lubrication. Characteristics. Types of Lubricants - Bearings.

TOPIC V Bearing calculation - Bearing life - Influence of the environment and lubrication on bearing life - Bearing safety and adjusted life - Selection of bearing type based on load and speed, for a determined life
TOPIC VI Brakes and clutches - Useful use of friction: Materials - Types of brakes and clutches. Systems - Dimensioning.

TOPIC VII Flexible elements special belts - Belts, characteristics of the materials used in their manufacture - Toothed belts - Tension ratio between branches - Calculation of transmitted torque - Dimensioning of the belt type and number based on project needs.

TOPIC VIII Extension to the calculation of Mechanical Springs - Helical springs (Definition) - Specific characteristics of the materials used in their manufacture - Spring constant, commonly accepted values - Helical springs, subjected to tension – compression. Stresses and deformations. - Critical frequency of helical springs - Helical springs, with torsional stresses. Stresses and deformations - Leaf springs. Dimensioning and effort assessment - Disc springs (Bellville)
assessment_rules: To average the grades of the assessable tests and pass the subject, a minimum passing grade of 5 must be obtained in each of them.
